title: Governing AI in Financial Crime Compliance
summary: Applying model risk management to AI-driven financial crime tools, so that the firm can explain, validate, monitor and defend them, and avoid unfair or discriminatory outcomes.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: Applying model risk management to AI-driven financial crime tools, so that the firm can explain, validate, monitor and defend them, and avoid unfair or discriminatory outcomes.
Learning Objectives: Apply model risk management to AML, screening and fraud models
Evaluate explainability, human oversight and audit trails
Assess bias and de-risking effects on customers
Syllabus: Model inventory, validation and performance monitoring
Explainability for investigators, auditors and supervisors
Vendor tools, data quality and third-party dependency
Bias, financial exclusion and unwarranted de-risking
Intended Audience: MLROs, deputy MLROs and heads of financial crime compliance
Financial crime, AML, sanctions and fraud analysts, investigators and team leaders
Compliance, risk, data and technology staff who design, validate or run financial crime systems
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Experience of AML, sanctions or fraud compliance in a regulated firm is helpful. No data science background is required.
Core Reading: FATF, International Standards on Combating Money Laundering and the Financing of Terrorism and Proliferation: The FATF Recommendations (as updated)
FATF, Opportunities and Challenges of New Technologies for AML/CFT (2021)
